extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, recipients, PD/PIs, and institutional grant administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for post-award administration of NIH grants, including audits, enforcement remedies, closeout, appeals, and multiple PD/PI application requirements. Guidance is aimed at organizations, PD/PIs, and grant management officials responsible for complying with NIH award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of SF-SAC and Single Audit package
rubrics_metrics.description: The data collection form (SF-SAC) and a copy of the Single Audit reporting package must be submitted electronically to the FAC at the address provided in Part III.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A senior level representative of the auditee must sign a statement included as part of the data collection confirming compliance, accuracy, absence of protected PII, and authorization for FAC to make the reporting package publicly available (with an Indian tribe/tribal organization exception allowing opt-out of FAC publication but requiring direct submission to pass-through entities and public inspection unless restricted by federal statute/regulation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit finding reporting to HHS/NIH
rubrics_metrics.description: If the schedule of findings and questioned costs discloses an audit finding related to an HHS or NIH award or reports status of any such prior audit finding, the FAC will provide copies of the audit report to NEARC, OIG, HHS (and NEARC will distribute them within HHS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit reports should not be sent directly to the GMO. The threshold for reporting questioned costs is described in 2 CFR Part 200.516.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely resolution of audit findings and 30-day response requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must follow a systematic method for ensuring timely and appropriate resolution of audit findings and recommendations; recipients usually are allowed 30 days from the date of request to respond to the responsible audit resolution official (Action Official).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit timely responses may result in cost disallowance or other actions by NIH or HHS. At completion of audit resolution, the recipient will be notified of the Action Official's final decision and may appeal if covered by NIH/HHS grant appeals procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely submission of required audits (2 CFR Part 200, Subpart F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must submit required 2 CFR Part 200, Subpart F audits within the time limits specified in the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If delinquent, NIH may take actions that may result in loss of Federal funds. No audit costs will be allowed as indirect or direct costs to Federal awards if required audits have not been completed or conducted in accordance with 2 CFR Part 200, Subpart F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on allowing audit costs without compliant audits
rubrics_metrics.description: No audit costs will be allowed either as indirect costs or direct costs to Federal awards if the required audits have not been completed or have not been conducted in accordance with the provisions of 2 CFR Part 200, Subpart F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Cost Considerations—Allowability of Costs/Activities—Selected Items of Cost for further allowability guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of Specific Award Conditions by GMO
rubrics_metrics.description: During grant performance, the GMO may include specific award conditions in the grant award to require correction of identified financial or administrative deficiencies to protect NIH’s interests and effect positive change in performance or compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When imposed, GMO will notify the recipient in writing of the nature of the conditions, reasons, corrective action needed, time allowed, and method for requesting reconsideration. See 42 CFR Part 52.9 and 2 CFR Part 200.339.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of PD/PI or senior/key personnel approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH awarding IC may withdraw approval of the PD/PI or other senior/key personnel named in the NoA if there is a reasonable basis to conclude they are no longer qualified or competent to perform the research objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The awarding IC may request that the recipient designate a new PD/PI or other named senior/key personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary and generally non-appealable modification of award terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, the decision to modify the terms of an award (e.g., imposing specific award conditions) is discretionary on the part of the NIH awarding IC and is not appealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients will be notified in writing of imposed conditions and procedures for reconsideration, but modification decisions are ordinarily at IC discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for noncompliance (enumerated actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: When noncompliance cannot be remedied by specific conditions, NIH may take one or more actions: temporarily withhold payments; disallow costs; suspend or terminate the Federal award in part or entirety; initiate suspension or debarment proceedings per 2 CFR Part 180; withhold further Federal funds (new awards or continuation funding); pursue other legally available remedies in consultation with HHS Office of General Counsel, NIH Branch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory procedures for suspension and termination are specified in 2 CFR Parts 200.340–200.343.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of termination
rubrics_metrics.description: An NIH award may be terminated: (1) By NIH for recipient failure to comply with terms; (2) By NIH with the consent of the recipient (bilateral termination); (3) By the recipient upon written notification (subject to NIH determination regarding remaining portion); (4) By NIH pursuant to award terms if the award no longer effectuates program goals or agency priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH must provide written notification of termination including reasons, effective date, and portion to be terminated. See 2 CFR Part 200.341.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination notification content and SAM.gov reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: When an award is terminated for material failure to comply, the notification must state: (1) the termination will be reported to the OMB-designated integrity and performance system accessible through SAM.gov; (2) info will be available in SAM.gov for five years then archived; (3) agencies must consider this info for future awards exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold; (4) recipient may comment on SAM.gov information; (5) NIH may consider recipient comments when determining qualification for future awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon termination, NIH will provide information required by FFATA to USAspending.gov and update other government-wide systems as required by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension before termination and immediate termination for public health
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH generally will suspend (rather than immediately terminate) a grant and allow corrective action, but may terminate if corrective action is not taken during suspension. NIH may immediately terminate when necessary to protect public health and welfare from a serious deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination for failure to carry out approved project may be appealed under NIH and HHS grant appeals procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withholding of support (reasons and appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Withholding of support (not making a non-competing continuation award) may occur because: adequate Federal funds are not available; recipient failed to show satisfactory progress; recipient failed to meet terms/conditions of a previous award; or continued funding would not be in the Federal government's best interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient may appeal NIH’s determination to deny (withhold) a non-competing continuation award for failure to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other enforcement actions (alternate remedies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on deficiency nature, NIH may convert payment methods (advance to reimbursement), disallow costs for noncompliant activities, suspend or debar organization/individual under 45 CFR Part 76, or pursue civil action or other legal remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension under 45 CFR Part 76 (Debarment and Suspension) is separate from award suspension as a post-award remedy. Debarment/suspension as eligibility criteria are addressed elsewhere in pre-award processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative recovery of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH may identify and administratively recover funds paid to a recipient at any time during the grant life cycle for reasons such as cost disallowances, unobligated balances, unpaid required matching/cost sharing, or other circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on repayment of grant funds unrelated to audit findings is on the Grants Compliance and Oversight page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debt collection procedures and interest accrual
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collection is governed by Federal Claims Collection Act and related statutes; NIH is required to collect debts and, except where prohibited, to charge interest on delinquent debts. Debts are delinquent if not paid within 30 days from the date the debt notification is mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delinquent debts are subject to interest, administrative cost charges, and penalties. If recipient appeals an adverse monetary determination under specified regs, interest accrues but assessment is deferred pending final decision; if appeal fails, interest is charged beginning with debt notification date. Interest computed using prevailing Treasury rate per 45 CFR Part 30.13(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout deadline and unilateral closeout
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must submit final FFR, Final RPPR, and Final Invention Statement and Certification within 120 calendar days of the end of the period of performance (reports become overdue on day 121). NIH may initiate unilateral closeout if recipient does not provide timely accurate closeout reports or respond to NIH reconciliation requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If recipient fails to submit closeout documents within a year of project period end date, NIH will unilaterally close the award and report failure to comply in SAM.gov. Failure to correct recurring reporting problems may lead to corrective actions, withholding further awards, suspension or termination. Closeout does not cancel requirements for property accountability, record retention, or financial accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention period after closeout
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients generally must retain financial and programmatic records, supporting documents, statistical records, and all other records required by the grant or pertinent to a grant for a period of 3 years from the date the annual FFR is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following closeout, recipient remains obligated to return funds due as a result of later refunds, corrections, or other transactions; the Federal government may recover amounts based on audit results covering any part of the grant period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subrecipient closeout reporting deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: A subrecipient must submit to the recipient, no later than 90 calendar days (or earlier date as agreed in the subaward) after the project period end date, all reports as required by the terms and conditions of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Federal Financial Report (Final FFR) required circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: A final FFR is required for any award that is terminated; any award transferred to a new recipient; or any award (including SNAP awards) which will not be extended through award of a new competitive segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final FFRs must be electronically submitted through the Payment Management System, cover the entire competitive segment or funded portion before termination, indicate exact unobligated fund balance, and have no discrepancies between Federal share of expenditures on the final FFR and net cash disbursements in PMS Transactions section. Reconciliation prior to PMS submission is recipient's responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for approval of a revised final FFR
rubrics_metrics.description: When a revised final FFR results in additional claims by the recipient, NIH will consider approval subject to minimum criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum criteria: recipient must indicate why revision is necessary and implement internal controls to preclude recurrence; charge must be otherwise allowable under grant provisions; there must be an unobligated balance sufficient to cover the claim; funds must still be available for use; NIH must receive the revised final FFR within one year of original due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final RPPR requirements and Interim-RPPR for pending Type 2
rubrics_metrics.description: A Final RPPR is required for any grant that is terminated and any award that will not be extended through award of a new competitive segment. If a competitive renewal (Type 2) application has been submitted, the recipient must submit an Interim-RPPR while the renewal is under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Type 2 is funded, NIH will treat the Interim-RPPR as the annual performance report for the final year of the previous segment; if not funded, it will be treated as the Final RPPR. Final RPPRs should be prepared per RPPR Instructions on the NIH RPPR website and any award-specific final progress report instructions (SBIR/STTR Phase II instructions in RPPR Section 7.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Invention Statement and Certification (HHS 568) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must submit a Final Invention Statement and Certification (HHS 568), whether or not the project results in subject inventions, and whether or not inventions were previously reported. The HHS 568 must list all inventions conceived or first reduced to practice during the project and be signed by an AOR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form should cover period from original effective date of support through completion/termination and be submitted to the NIH awarding IC. If none, the form must indicate 'None.' Certain activity codes are exempt from current HHS 568 requirement—contact awarding IC for specifics. HHS 568 does not relieve obligation to promptly report inventions directly to NIH as required by award terms. Copies of form available on iEdison and Forms Directory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission of closeout documents
rubrics_metrics.description: All closeout documents must be submitted electronically via eRA Commons (Final RPPR and Final Invention Statement) or PMS (Final FFR), as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH no longer accepts paper or e-mail submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH first-level grant appeals procedure and exhaustion before DAB
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS permits recipients to appeal certain post-award adverse administrative decisions. NIH has established a first-level grant appeal procedure that must be exhausted before the recipient may file an appeal with the Departmental Appeals Board (DAB). NIH assumes jurisdiction for specified adverse determinations set forth in 42 CFR Part 50.404.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal notification of an adverse determination will contain a statement of the recipient's appeal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse determinations under NIH jurisdiction for first-level appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will assume jurisdiction for adverse determinations: termination of a grant for failure to carry out approved project or comply with law/terms; determination that an expenditure is not allowable or recipient failed to account for funds; denial (withholding) of a non-competing continuation for failure to comply with terms of a previous award; determination that a grant is void (invalid because not authorized or fraudulently obtained).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for recipient's request for NIH review
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first-level appeal, the recipient must submit a request for review to the NIH official specified in the notification, detailing the nature of the disagreement and providing supporting documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request for review must include a copy of the adverse determination, identify the issue(s) in dispute, contain a full statement of recipient's position with pertinent facts and reasons, and provide copies of documents supporting the claim (42 CFR Part 50.406(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for NIH appeal request and DAB appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient's request to NIH for review must be submitted no later than 30 days after the written notification of the adverse determination is received (extensions may be granted for good cause). If NIH decision is adverse or request rejected on jurisdictional grounds, the recipient may submit a request to the DAB within 30 days after receiving the final NIH decision, provided preliminary appeal processes required by regulation have been exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 42 CFR Part 50.406(a) and 45 CFR Part 16.3(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: DAB jurisdiction for disputes related to cost allocations and rates
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to previously listed adverse determinations, the DAB is the single level of appeal for disputes related to establishment of indirect cost rates, research patient care rates, and certain other cost allocations used in determining amounts to be reimbursed under NIH grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such determinations may be made by an HHS official other than the GMO and may affect NIH and other HHS grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with program goals and termination for programmatic reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH may terminate awards, to the extent authorized by law, if an award no longer effectuates program goals or agency priorities. These termination actions are not terminations for noncompliance and are not appealable under 2 CFR 200.342 or 42 CFR 50, subpart D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued funding for an award is contingent upon availability of appropriated funds, recipient satisfactory performance, compliance with award terms, and ongoing alignment with program goals or agency priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple PD/PI equal authority and shared responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple PD/PI awards allow multidisciplinary efforts and collaboration through a team of scientists under a single grant award; all PD/PIs share equally the authority and responsibility for leading and directing the project, intellectually and logistically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of more than one PD/PI diminishes neither responsibility nor accountability of any individual PD/PI. Each PD/PI is responsible and accountable to the applicant organization (or appropriate collaborating organization) for proper conduct of the project, including submission of required reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant organization responsibility for PD/PI signatures and assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant/recipient organization is responsible for securing and retaining required written assurance signatures from each identified PD/PI on all applications, post-submission information, progress reports, and post-award prior approval requests and must make these signatures available to NIH or other authorized DHHS or Federal officials upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional information available at the NIH Multiple Principal Investigators website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and exceptions for multiple PD/PI option
rubrics_metrics.description: Most award mechanisms submitted through Grants.gov permit multiple PD/PIs, with exceptions where multiple PD/PIs are not appropriate (individual fellowships and career awards, dissertation grants R36, Pioneer Awards DP1, Construction Grants C06/UC6, Grants for Repair/Renovation G20, Shared Instrumentation Grants S10). SBIR/STTR applicants may use multiple PD/PI option with program-specific requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For active awards, changing from multiple PD/PI to single PD/PI or changes in number/makeup require prior approval of funding IC (see Change in Status).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision and rationale for submitting multiple PD/PI application
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to submit a multiple PD/PI application is that of the applicant organization and the PD/PIs, and should be consistent with the scientific goals of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single applicant organization may designate multiple PD/PIs from itself or from multiple institutions. Multiple organizations may not submit the same multiple PD/PI application.

rubrics_metrics.name: PD/PI qualifications and defined roles
rubrics_metrics.description: All PD/PIs must be qualified and have appropriate expertise to serve as a PD/PI and the appropriate level of authority and responsibility to direct the project or program as part of the leadership team; each PD/PI must have a defined role on the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no limit on the number of PD/PIs and no minimum person-months requirement except for STTR applicants where each PD/PI must commit minimum effort of 1.2 calendar months (10%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact PD/PI designation and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant organization must designate one PD/PI as the Contact PD/PI to serve as primary point of contact; Contact PD/PI must be listed first and associated with the applicant organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact PD/PI is responsible for communication between PD/PIs and NIH, assembly of application materials, coordination of progress reports; on complex projects the Contact PD/PI may request additional effort for coordination responsibilities if necessary. Contact PD/PI has no special authorities within the leadership team.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons registration requirement for PD/PIs
rubrics_metrics.description: All PD/PIs must have established eRA Commons accounts with a PI role prior to application submission. When multiple PD/PIs are at different organizations, all organizations must also be registered in eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Contact PD/PI is at a different institution than the applicant organization, the applicant organization must affiliate the contact PD/PI with their institution. Beyond the contact PD/PI, not all PD/PIs need to be affiliated with the applicant organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership Plan requirement for multiple PD/PI applications
rubrics_metrics.description: All multiple PD/PI applications are required to include a Leadership Plan to facilitate and enhance scientific productivity and establish decision-making processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan must describe rationale for multiple PD/PI approach; governance and organizational structure including communication plans, process for scientific decisions, procedures for resolving conflicts; delineate roles and administrative/technical/scientific responsibilities for PD/PIs, including responsibilities for human subject studies or vertebrate animal studies as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: New investigator classification for multiple PD/PI applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple PD/PI applications may designate senior and new investigators, including early stage investigators. The application will be considered a new investigator application only when all PD/PIs meet NIH definition of new investigator; similarly for early stage investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serving as a PD/PI on a substantial independent multiple PD/PI research award is equivalent to serving as a PD/PI on a substantial independent single PD/PI research award for classification purposes. Adding a new investigator to an active substantial independent research award does not change their new investigator status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-project application PD/PI vs subproject lead distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: When NOFO for Multi-project applications allows multiple PD/PIs, applications may include multiple lead investigators for subprojects as well as multiple PD/PIs for entire program. Do not confuse lead investigators of a subproject with PD/PIs of the entire application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead investigators of subprojects/components are not automatically considered PD/PIs of entire application. When a lead investigator is also a PD/PI of the entire program, that individual must be specifically designated as a PD/PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget rules for multiple PD/PI applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, multiple PD/PI applications will submit a single budget for the entire project (applies to modular and detailed budgets). The $250,000 modular budget threshold is for the entire project, not per PD/PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When PD/PIs are at different institutions, standard consortium budget instructions apply. Applicants may include budget allocation information for specific PD/PIs in the Leadership Plan; in the event of an award, requested allocations may be reflected as a term in the NoA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal/resubmission changes in PD/PI model
rubrics_metrics.description: A renewal or resubmission may change from single to multiple PD/PIs or change the number/makeup of multiple PD/PIs, but the applicant must provide a rationale for the change and include the required Leadership Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A previously submitted multiple PD/PI application may change to a single PD/PI in a renewal/resubmission if a rationale is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing revision applications and Contact PD/PI requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A competing revision to an existing Multiple PD/PI grant must be submitted using the same Contact PD/PI as the parent grant and may propose changes in the Leadership Plan or composition (adding/removing PD/PIs) with rationale for changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A competitive revision to a single PD/PI grant may propose multiple PD/PIs provided a Leadership Plan is included.
